plan: [ This is a private-values second-price (Vickrey) auction with i.i.d. uniform values and rational opponents. The dominant strategy is to bid truthfully: bidding above value risks negative payoff if I win against a slightly higher second bid; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. No history to exploit and only 1 round, so no strategic shading or signaling matters. My value is 47 (near the top of 0–49), so bid exactly 47 to maximize expected profit. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. It guarantees winning whenever your value is the highest and paying the second-highest bid, which maximizes expected profit. Any bid shading risks losing when winning would have been profitable and does not lower the payment conditional on winning. With value 33 (uniform draws 0–49), bid 33 to capture all positive-surplus opportunities without overpaying. No history effects matter in a single round; ties are random, and truth-telling remains optimal. ]

[ This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: it avoids losses from overbidding (winning and paying above value) and avoids missed surplus from underbidding (losing when I should win). With three bidders and $0.1 increments, set bid to my exact value to ensure I win whenever the second-highest bid is below my value and pay that second-highest bid. There’s only one round, so no learning or signaling considerations. Bid truthfully at 36.0. ]
